new_statements.quote: There is no fully-developed pitch-accent system. However, in sequences of H-toned syllables within a word that is pronounced in isolation or otherwise in prepausal (clause-final) position, the first such syllable is phonetically stressed and this entails a partial drop in pitch on the remaining syllables. This is particularly conspicuous with final Cv: syllables, which are very common for nouns and adjectives. For example, pédé: ‘sheep-Sg’ is heard as [ˈpédē(:)] in isolation, with mid pitch on the second syllable and no conspicuous prolongation of its vowel. In clause-medial position, on the other hand, it is heard as [ˈpédé:] with level H-tone and more noticeable length on the final vowel.
new_statements.citation: Heath, Jeffrey. 2023. A Grammar of Tebul Ure (Dogon, Mali). University of Michigan, April 2023. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7850338. §3.1.2 'Stress and accent', p. 13.

new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (537 pp., text layer, pdfinfo title "prefinal black Heath_Tebul_Ure_grammar", created 2023-04-20; title page "A Grammar of Tebul Ure (Dogon, Mali) / Jeffrey Heath / University of Michigan / April 2023"). extracted text of PDF p. 30 = printed p. 13 shows the heading "3.1.2 Stress and accent" followed by the quoted passage word for word, including the examples pédé: 'sheep-Sg' = [ˈpédē(:)] in isolation vs [ˈpédé:] clause-medially, and the following paragraph on the medial vowel of CvCvCv being the weak metrical position (syncope, §3.4.3.1). Corroborating locators all check out: §2.1.2 Prosody, printed p. 5 (PDF 22): "TU does distinguish H.H from H.L, so it does not have a pitch-accent…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tebul Ure is a tone language (lexical stem melodies /H/, /LH/, /HL/, /LHL/; no /L/ melody, single H peak per stem). Stress is phonetic, not contrastive: in a word spoken in isolation or clause-finally, the first H-toned syllable of a run of H syllables is stressed and the remaining H syllables are lowered to mid pitch; for /H/-melodic (all-high) stems this is a 'phonetic primary accent on the initial syllable' (§3.6.1.2, p. 36; §2.1.2, p. 5 'phonetic stress on the first of two or more H-toned syllables'). For /LH/-type stems the stressed syllable is the (first) H-toned one, i.e. stress follows the tone peak. Metrically, the medial syllable of CvCvCv is the weak position (short high vowels syncopate there, §3.1.2).
new_statements.exceptions: The stress/pitch-lowering effect is described for prepausal (isolation, clause-final) position; clause-medially the H tones stay level (though Heath still transcribes [ˈpédé:]). Heath notes the language is 'intermediate' between a classic Dogon tone system and the Donno So / Dogul Dom pitch-accent type but explicitly says it does not have a pitch-accent system since H.H and H.L remain distinct.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (stems/words in isolation or in prepausal/clause-final position); examples are citation forms of nouns and adjectives. Interaction with the tonosyntactic tone overlays on multi-word NPs is not discussed in the stress section.
new_statements.identity_note: Heath 2023 describes Tebul Ure (TU; = 'Oru yille' of Calame-Griaule 1956, Glottolog tebu1239, ISO dtu) as a single language, fieldwork 2010-2023 with a speaker from the main TU villages near Yanda, Mali. The scan's 'unreachable' verdict is superseded: the full reference grammar is open access on Zenodo (2023 final version; a 2020 preliminary draft, also on Zenodo, lacks the stress section). Glottolog's Morse-Gagné 1997 entry for this glottocode is a misassignment (Middle English text 'Ure Lauerd').
